scenario_description: Lena receives advance notice of an optional utility program that rewards households for running dishwashers and laundry after 8:00 PM, but event1 lacks the personalized terms needed to judge whether changing the household routine would be worthwhile. At event2, Lena tells Maya that she would like to participate if their offer provides at least $10 per month without a fee, yet intervention is still premature because their actual offer has not arrived. Event3 makes the opportunity sufficiently observable at a non-final checkpoint: the personalized offer meets Lena's stated conditions, her dishwasher record shows that its delay-start control can move cycles past 8:00 PM, and the utility permits enrollment by a simple email reply. A proactive agent can enroll Lena, create a practical delayed-dishwasher and Sunday-laundry schedule, and coordinate Maya's unloading chore around the new timing. Later events confirm that no equipment or landlord approval is required, show that Maya can accommodate the routine, and establish that the household is still missing credits under its unchanged schedule. The program remains optional, but using it could earn about $15 per month without reducing necessary appliance use.

parameter.subject: Personal Home Flex offer coming soon
parameter.body: We are reviewing your account for Home Flex, an optional program that gives monthly bill credits when most dishwasher and laundry cycles occur after 8:00 PM. Your personalized offer, including the credit amount and participation terms, will arrive within two days. No action can be taken until that offer is issued.

parameter.content: The electric company may offer us a credit for running the dishwasher and laundry later. We normally start the dishwasher around 6:45 after dinner, and I usually start Sunday laundry around 5:00. If their actual offer is at least $10 a month, has no fee, and does not require new equipment, I would like to join and adjust those routines.

parameter.subject: Your $15 monthly Home Flex offer
parameter.body: Your account MES-ORTIZ-4826 qualifies for a $15 credit each month that at least 80% of your dishwasher and laundry cycles begin after 8:00 PM. There is no enrollment fee, no change to your electricity rate, and no required equipment. To enroll for the next monthly cycle, reply to this email with ENROLL and your account reference MES-ORTIZ-4826. You may leave the program at any time.

parameter.subject: Home Flex scheduling clarification
parameter.body: Home Flex only changes when you choose to run appliances. It does not require installation, inspection, or a property-owner authorization. Dishwasher delay-start cycles qualify based on their actual start time, and laundry may be done on any day as long as qualifying cycles begin after 8:00 PM.

parameter.content: Starting the dishwasher later is fine with me. I can unload it before breakfast instead of right after dinner, and I can still fold the Sunday laundry the next morning if you wash it after 8.

Tonight's dishwasher was started at 6:45 again because I have not enrolled or set its delay control yet. The utility offer is still available, so we could begin the later routine once those steps are arranged.

parameter.name: maintenance_guide.txt
parameter.content:
Dishwasher delay-start note
The Westlake DW-420 delay button postpones the beginning of a cycle in one-hour steps. After selecting the normal cycle, press Delay until the display shows the desired number of hours, then press Start and close the door. The dishwasher remains off until the delayed start time.
